title: Can a little weight balance a big one?
objectives: Notice that distance from the pivot changes a weight's turning effect.
Balance unequal weights by changing their positions.
Explain a new arrangement using both weight and distance.

characters.genius: Ask one useful question and use observed model results.
characters.rookie: Make a tentative testable guess, then revise it from evidence.

misconception.hypothesis: The side with more blocks must always go down.
misconception.resolution: Where the blocks are placed also matters.

model.result: left_score == right_score ? balanced : left_score > right_score ? left_down : right_down
assumptions: Symmetric beam centered at the pivot
Distances measured from pivot in equal units
model.rendering_note: Bounded eased tilt illustrates direction only. Reset each trial to horizontal before release. Do not represent the angle as a physical measurement or integrate an unverified dynamics model.

steps.prompt: What might happen if we move the single block farther from the middle?
Try moving the single block one notch farther.
Can you tell Rookie why moving the block helped?

rubric.recognizes_distance: The child mentions being farther from the middle or pivot.
rubric.connects_weight_and_distance: The child connects how much weight with where it is placed.
rubric.uncertain_transcript: Do not grade; offer a tap or a demonstration.

steps.prompt: Can you balance this arrangement by moving the single block?
Both the weight and its distance from the middle matter.

invariants: Counts and distances remain integers within the declared limits.
Readout, narration facts and visible direction use the same computed result.
Every mutation checks expected_scene_version and increments scene_version.
An action_id is applied at most once.
A manual drag invalidates queued explanations based on an older scene state.
product_scope: Open-ended tutoring accepts arbitrary runtime questions. This fixture is not a lesson catalogue or required teaching sequence.
contract_note: This legacy fixture uses scene_version as its mutation counter. Generated explainer packages instead separate scene_version from state_revision; use the service tool/runtime schemas.
phases_policy: Optional fixture-only sequence; not the open-ended planner policy.
